title: Regional suitability scoring and warm snapshot replay checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During regional congestion or outages we currently choose fallback regions by coarse heuristics (priority list + health probes). This leads to suboptimal cutovers: increased tail latency, model variant mismatches, and cold KV cache penalties. Goal: implement a deterministic regional suitability score and a lightweight warm-snapshot replay mechanism so standby regions can be validated and primed continuously without impacting production SLAs.
background: We have multiple layers that influence cutover quality: (1) network latency matrix (2) GPU capacity headroom by tier (3) model variant compatibility (quantized vs full-precision) and (4) KV cache 'warmth' for popular prompt prefixes. Current readiness checks are mostly liveness/instance-level. We need a fleet-level, route-aware readiness signal to drive smart routing policies and automated failover orchestration.
design_summary: 1) Compute a Regional Suitability Score (RSS) per region and per logical route. RSS = weighted(sum(latency_p50_normalized, capacity_headroom, model_variant_compatibility, cache_warmth_score, recent_error_rate)). Weights are configurable by route/tier. 2) Implement Warm Snapshot Replay (WSR): sample <0.5% of requests (synthetic shadowing with traffic-safety limits) and replay them against candidate standby region model variants and cache priming pipelines; collect latency/token-cost delta, model output diffs, and success signals. 3) Feed RSS and WSR pass/fail badges into the routing decision engine and the orchestrator to enable: - tier-aware region selection - adaptive traffic ramping during cutover - automatic model-variant fallback mapping
acceptance_criteria: RSS computed per region/route and visible in console for 3 pilot routes
WSR can be configured to target a set of standby regions and model variants without affecting production requests
Cutover simulations using recorded traffic show <10% additional tail latency and <2% increase in token cost compared to baseline for pilot routes
Automated region choice in canary failovers picks RSS top-2 region and ramps traffic according to plan
Telemetry surfaces root-cause (latency vs capacity vs model mismatch) for each readiness failure
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement RSS prototype service that consumes existing telemetry (p50/p95, available GPU slots, model variant table, cache-hit stats)
Phase 2 (2 weeks): build WSR worker that performs safe shadow replays with explicit rate limits and opaque token scrubbing; results persisted to a verdict stream
Phase 3 (1 week): integrate RSS/WSR into routing decision layer with feature flag gating and console controls
Phase 4 (1 week): run canary simulations and staged rollouts for three pilot routes (internal search, chat-assist, embeddings)
telemetry_requirements: Per-region per-route RSS components emitted every 30s
WSR replay events with tags: original_req_id, route, source_region, target_region, model_variant, latency_delta_ms, cache_warmth_delta, output_checksum_diff
SLO dashboards: fraction of traffic routed to non-top-RSS regions, cutover ramp profiles, and rollback incidents
Alert: RSS_drop > threshold for a region tier affecting >5% production traffic
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal-only feature flag (no routing effect) — gather baseline for 48h
Stage 1: enable WSR sampling to standby regions for pilot routes (0.1% of traffic), log-only
Stage 2: enable RSS-driven routing for pilot routes in canary mode (10% of cutover events use new selector)
Stage 3: full pilot rollout for 3 routes with throttled ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) over 72h windows
Stage 4: iterate weights and thresholds based on telemetry, prepare runbook and handoff to SRE
qa_checks: Unit tests for RSS calculation and weight config parsing
Integration tests for WSR worker with synthetic replay traffic and mock model variants
Chaos test: simulate elevated P95 in primary region and assert orchestrator selects the higher RSS region and ramps per plan
End-to-end smoke: confirm no PII leakage during replay (token scrubber verified)
risks: Replay traffic could accidentally increase cost if sampling configuration is incorrect (mitigate with hard caps)
Model-variant output diffs may be noisy; risk of false negatives leading to unnecessary cutovers (mitigate with diff thresholds and ensemble heuristics)
Complexity in operationally tuning weights per-route; requires good defaults and conservative rollouts
Latency to compute RSS if upstream telemetry stalls; fallback to conservative priority list required
runbook_notes: If RSS suddenly drops for top region: immediate circuit-breaker to soft-fail routing to next region and page on-call SRE
If WSR shows persistent model-variant regressions (>5% mismatched outputs for 24h): pin to compatible variant and notify model-onboarding team
Use console controls to temporarily disable WSR for a region undergoing maintenance
